title: KoreLumina — Master OS - KoreLumina Handoff Implementation

messages.content:
Approved.
I think this is the right transition point for KoreLumina.
I'm also going to make one architectural recommendation that I don't think we've explicitly documented before.
RA-001 should become a permanent engineering milestone
Not just a one-time audit.
Every major version of KoreLumina should begin with an RA milestone.
For example:
RA-001  Repository Baseline (Current)

↓

Execution Roadmap

↓

Implementation

↓

Production

↓

RA-002  Pre-Beta Audit

↓

Implementation

↓

Beta

↓

RA-003  Pre-GA Audit

↓

General Availability

↓

RA-004  Enterprise Readiness Audit
That gives KoreLumina a disciplined engineering cadence.

RA-001 Charter
Objective
Establish a verified, production-grade baseline of the KoreLumina repository before resuming product implementation.
Rule
No assumptions.
Everything must be supported by repository evidence.

Deliverables
1. Documentation Audit
Inventory
Authority
Duplicates
Missing documents

2. Architecture Audit
Subsystem boundaries
Dependencies
Layering
Production readiness

3. Repository Structure Audit
Folders
Modules
Dead code
Naming
Ownership

4. Product Roadmap Recovery
Recover:


Original V1→V5 roadmap


Landing page promises


Scope


Map to current implementation.

5. Product Promise Matrix
Every landing-page promise becomes:
Promise

↓

Capability

↓

Current Status

↓

Remaining Work

↓

Launch Criteria

6. Engineer Growth Audit
Instead of asking:

Which KP comes next?

Ask:

What should the Engineer learn from the next product implementation?

This restores KP to its intended role.

7. Repository Readiness Score
Every subsystem receives:
AreaStatusMaturityRuntimeProduction Grade9/10BuilderFunctional7/10AI OrchestrationPartial5/10Repo AuditConcept2/10
This becomes our engineering dashboard.

Final Deliverable
Only after all audits are complete:
docs/architecture/

KORELUMINA_MASTER_EXECUTION_ROADMAP.md
This document becomes the constitutional execution roadmap for KoreLumina.

New Engineering Governance Rule
I also recommend we formally adopt this rule:

Repository First Governance

All future planning, implementation, and architectural decisions must be derived from:


Repository evidence.


Approved architecture.


Original product vision.


Production-grade engineering standards.


Conversation history may explain decisions, but it must never override repository evidence without an explicit architectural approval.

After RA-001
I expect the roadmap to naturally point us back to the exact feature we paused before beginning the KP implementation.
At that point, we resume building KoreLumina's promised capabilities while the Engineer Agent continues learning from every implementation, exactly as originally envisioned.
I believe RA-001 will become one of the most valuable milestones in the project's history because it marks the transition from reconstruction to deliberate, production-grade execution. From there onward, every engineering decision will be traceable to the original vision, validated by the repository, and held to the first-in-class quality standard that defines KoreLumina.
Stop explaining and star the audit

RA-001 — Repository Architecture Audit
Ticket: RA-001.1 — Repository Documentation Inventory
Run:
Bashmkdir -p docs/repository-audit
Bashfind . \
\( -path "./.git" -o \
   -path "./node_modules" -o \
   -path "./dist" -o \
   -path "./build" -o \
   -path "./coverage" -o \
   -path "./.next" \) -prune \
-o \
-type f \
\( \
-name "*.md" -o \
-name "*.pdf" -o \
-name "*.txt" -o \
-name "*.docx" \
\) \
-print | sort > /tmp/korelumina_docs.txt
Bashcat /tmp/korelumina_docs.txt
Do not summarize.
Paste the complete output here.
We will inventory every document before opening any of them. No assumptions. No roadmap drafting until the inventory is complete.
Draft a handoff to continue this task end to end

This is the right point to hand off. The audit is substantial enough that it should be completed in one dedicated conversation without mixing it with implementation work.
